text:
Dana Brooks: dropping a compact cohort warmup + canary feedback play for renewal-risk accounts. focused on segmented prefill, tiny canary, and automated feedback webhooks — copy/pasteable for SAs.
Hector Ruiz: nice. paste the customer-facing one-paragraph note and the ops checklist so SAs can send it directly.
Dana Brooks: copyable customer note: "Well run a small staged warmup for your assistant to improve latency and consistency. Step 1: run 3 representative prompts (we can provide examples) with prefill_tokens=1000, spacing=12s, 2 repeats each for a cohort of users. Step 2: well run a 5% canary of live traffic for 24h and monitor p95, cache_hit_rate, and user feedback. If p95 exceeds 850ms or user helpfulness <5/10 we will pause the rollout and revert to the previous variant. Please paste redwood.latency.p95 and redwood.cache.hit_ratio after warmup or share a dashboard screenshot."
Mina Park: ops checklist (short): 1) cohort_id: create cohort label (e.g., renewal-cohort-YYMMDD). 2) prefill: run for cohort prompts with prefill_tokens=1k, spacing=12s, 2 repeats. 3) canary: route 5% traffic for 24h. 4) thresholds: p95 > 850ms OR cache.hit_ratio p90 < 0.55 OR helpfulness <=5 -> rollback. 5) capture feedback via webhook (see snippet).
Owen Li: sample staggered prefill schedule for eng teams (keeps quota smooth): round 1: 20% of cohort prompts at t=0, round 2: 40% at t=5m, round 3: 40% at t=15m. run with <=2 concurrent clients.
Hector Ruiz: include a tiny one-question survey payload we can drop into the product or email. makes capture simple.
Mina Park: survey suggestion: {"question":"How helpful was the assistant in the last 24h? (0-10)", "field": "helpfulness"}. We recommend posting answers to the webhook below.
Owen Li: webhook example (POST target customers can accept or we can proxy):
POST /hooks/assistant-feedback  HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"account_id":"acct_ABC","cohort_id":"renewal-cohort-2309","timestamp":"2023-09-21T15:00:00Z","metrics":{"redwood.latency.p95":820,"redwood.cache.hit_ratio":0.62},"survey":{"helpfulness":7,"comment":"Looks better today"}}

Note: webhook payload keys we recommend: account_id, cohort_id, timestamp, metrics.*, survey.*.
Dana Brooks: tiny rollout guardrails for SAs: 1) run the prefill, confirm cache_hit p90 >= 0.55, 2) start canary at 5% and check p95 after 2h and 24h, 3) if helpfulness <=5 or metrics breach, pause and revert model variant. Also log the first 48h token burn in renewal notes.
Hector Ruiz: ops healthcheck bash snippet to share with customers:
#!/bin/bash
API_KEY=$REDWOOD_KEY
METRIC_URL="https://api.redwood.ai/v1/metrics?query=redwood.cache.hit_ratio&window=1h&account=acct_ABC"
val=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "$METRIC_URL" | jq '.p90')
if (( $(echo "$val >= 0.55" | bc -l) )); then
  echo "cache warm"
  exit 0
else
  echo "cache cold"
  exit 1
fi

Owen Li: small prefill curl for eng (cohort mode):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefill-cohort 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"cohort_id":"renewal-cohort-2309","model":"assist-highp","samples":[{"prompt":"<promptA>","tokens":1000},{"prompt":"<promptB>","tokens":1000}],"stagger_schedule": [0,300,900] }'

Mina Park: telemetry keys we ask customers to paste or webhook: redwood.latency.p95, redwood.cache.hit_ratio, redwood.stream_gap_p90, cs.cohort_id, cs.prefill_round. Also capture survey.helpfulness and survey.comment.
Dana Brooks: final next steps: I'll publish the runbook entry and a 2-line TL;DR for #account-health. tagging @Owen for the prefill snippet and @Mina for webhook examples.
